source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Silicon Valley publishes 72 MW of IT capacity across 540,000 square feet of technical space in Santa Clara County. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 72 MW supports roughly 1,800 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation average, the same power supports roughly 7,200 racks. The arithmetic is an illustrative range, not an operator claim. The 540,000 square feet of technical space is large enough to accommodate dense cooling infrastructure alongside compute, which matters for high-heat GPU deployments, but the operator does not publish a per-rack power envelope or a cooling specification.

The campus holds a single published certification, LEED, which addresses the efficiency of the building envelope and mechanical systems and qualifies it as a facility built to a recognized energy standard. LEED says nothing about uptime tier, redundancy architecture, or security posture, none of which are published on the spec page this site has read.

Among the 103 data center facilities mapped in California, only five have published a megawatt figure to this site, totaling 170 MW across those five. EdgeCore Silicon Valley's 72 MW ranks second among those five, representing 42 percent of the published capacity this site has confirmed in the state. That share is a function of sparse disclosure, not a census of California capacity, and the true statewide installed base is substantially larger than the 170 MW this site has read.
